review.authorization_runtime_scope_assessment: The draft contract's authorization_scope_required enumerates exactly what the minted authorization must bind: exact 96 task IDs, allowed_modes=[e1], exact_k=8, required_skill_pre_sha256 (initial skill bcb738...), required_resolved_model deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813, identity_artifact_sha256 7fb73c09..., max_turns=10, max_output_tokens=4096, provider_budget (10/7680, claim-before-I/O, never released), status AUTHORIZED_E1, plus the three new runtime fields: runtime_python_executable, runtime_freeze_sha256, runtime_qualification_sha256. The orchestrator enforces runtime-scope drift fail-closed before actor spawn: it requires scope.runtime_python_executable == contract.runtime.python_executable, scope.runtime_freeze_sha256 == contract.runtime.freeze_sha256, and scope.runtime_qualification_sha256 == contract.runtime.qualification_sha256, in addition to task-set equality, mode, K, suite/split manifest SHAs, MindMemOS commit, and initial skill SHA. The actor runner independently revalidates resolved model, identity artifact SHA, max_turns, max_output_tokens, and provider budget limits against the authorization scope. This review has zero execution authority; the authorization must be minted separately and SHA-bound.
review.checkpoint_resume_assessment: V2.1 preserves the resume design: content-addressed trajectory refs (r17_trajectory_ref.json) are validated before reuse, including ledger/ref consistency checks (unit claim count equality and total counter non-regression) so a completed rollout is never re-run and never duplicates a provider call. Claims from ambiguous crashed calls are conservatively consumed: the ledger has no release path, _quarantine_partial preserves incomplete workdirs, and technical failure receipts persist adapter budget claims. The orchestrator acquires an exclusive O_EXCL lock, leaves it on failure for manual inspection, and on resume revalidates all completed stream receipts against the ledger before continuing missing streams only. No counter-reset or cross-contract reuse path exists: the ledger metadata binds the exact contract+authorization SHA pair, and any drift raises ProviderBudgetBindingError; a fresh contract gets a fresh run root and fresh ledger. The failed V2 ledger has 0 claims and is bound to the dead V2 contract/authorization pair, so it cannot be reused by V2.1.
review.failed_v2_contamination_assessment: The failure adjudication correctly establishes a pre-provider technical failure: ambient /usr/bin/python3 was used instead of the qualified venv, import failed at mindmemos_sdk->pydantic before any actor rollout, and the observed record shows 0 completed streams, 0 trajectory refs, 0 provider budget claims, 0 provider calls, 0 updater calls, 0 future-skill evaluations, and no mixed/rescue support inspection. Because no scientific outcome was observed, there is no outcome-selection contamination in minting a fresh contract. The adjudication mandates the failed V2 root/ledger/receipt/stale lock remain untouched and declares V2 non-retryable; V2.1 uses a fresh run root (e1-a-v31-pool-support-v2-1-20260828) distinct from the failed V2 root, and the technical_repair_gate requires the stale lock and failed root remain preserved. This is sufficient for a fresh contract without selection bias.
review.model_identity_assessment: Fresh V2.1 qualification binds deepseek-v4-pro to resolved deepseek-v4-pro-ga-260813 and kimi-k3 to kimi-k3, both with thinking_requested=disabled, provider_retry_limit=0, hidden_provider_retry_used=false, on the Ark Plan route, status PASS_CURRENT_REVIEW_TRANCHE. The adjudication explicitly documents the Kimi compatibility history (default-thinking smokes retained as incomplete-length protocol failures; passing call is a declared compatibility call with thinking disabled) and freezes identities only for this review tranche. The actor scientific path uses DeepSeek only (--model choices restricted to deepseek-v4-pro), and ArkPlanReactLLM raises on resolved-model drift; run_actor_rollout additionally requires all receipts' resolved_model to equal the required identity. The orchestrator validates the identity artifact SHA against the contract and the actor runner validates the authorization's identity_artifact_sha256 and required_resolved_model.
nonblocking_notes: The actor runner passes python_path=sys.executable to ReactAgentFactory; this is the venv python only because the orchestrator spawns the actor with the bound runtime python. If the actor runner were ever launched directly with an ambient python under a valid authorization, the MindMemOS import would fail closed (as V2 demonstrated), but a defense-in-depth check in the actor runner asserting sys.executable equals the authorization runtime scope would remove reliance on the orchestrator's binding. Not blocking because the only authorized launch path is the orchestrator and the failure mode is fail-closed.

The runtime qualification artifact records python_executable=/usr/bin/python3.12 as the base interpreter used by uv sync; this is the base interpreter, not the venv python, and the orchestrator correctly binds the venv python. No action needed.
The orchestrator's import smoke asserts openpyxl.__version__=='3.1.5' but does not pin a pydantic version assertion; the freeze SHA binding covers pydantic==2.13.4 immutability, so this is cosmetic.

Resume of a stream whose actor process was killed mid-stream relies on per-rollout content-addressed refs plus quarantine of partial workdirs; ambiguous provider claims are conservatively consumed, which may permanently burn budget on repeated crashes. This is the intended conservative semantics, not a defect.
This review has zero execution authority; it recommends at most minting a separately SHA-bound E1-A pool-generation authorization matching the draft contract's authorization_scope_required exactly.
